description: ENHANCING COMPUTATIONAL SKILL DEVELOPMENT IN BIOMEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH THROUGH ACQUISITION OF A HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING ENGINE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT FUNDS ARE REQUESTED FOR THE ACQUISITION OF A POWERWULF™ ZXR1 HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING (HPC) ENGINE TO ENHANCE COMPUTATIONAL SKILL DEVELOPMENT IN BIOMEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, DOMINGUEZ HILLS. THIS CENTRALIZED SHARED RESOURCE WILL SUPPORT THE RESEARCH OF NINE MAJOR USERS ACROSS FIVE DEPARTMENTS, INCLUDING DRS. ADEKUNLE AINA AND HORACE CROGMAN (PHYSICS), DR. SONAL SINGHAL (BIOLOGY), DRS. KARI PEDERSON AND KENNETH RODRIGUEZ (CHEMISTRY), DRS. YI WANG, ALEXANDER CHEN, AND CYNTHIA SÁNCHEZ TAPIA (MATHEMATICS), AND DR. SAHAR HOOSHMAND (COMPUTER SCIENCE). THIS SHARED RESOURCE WILL ALSO HELP INTEGRATE HANDS-ON TRAINING INTO FIVE CORE COURSES ACROSS FOUR DEPARTMENTS: BPH406 COMPUTATIONAL BIOPHYSICS; CHE420 ADVANCED APPLICATIONS IN CHEMISTRY; MAT 295 COMPUTING FOR MATHEMATICS; CSC 495/595 SPECIAL TOPICS MACHINE LEARNING AND DEEP LEARNING; AND MAT 171 MATHEMATICS FOR LIFE SCIENTISTS. IN TODAY’S DATA-DRIVEN BIOMEDICAL LANDSCAPE, MASTERY OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTING, LARGE-SCALE SIMULATION, AND REPRODUCIBLE PIPELINES IS ESSENTIAL. THE POWERWULF™ ZXR1 HPC ENGINE WILL ENABLE ACCESS TO TRAINING IN MODERN COMPUTATIONAL METHODS FOR BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATION, EMPOWERING OVER 50 STUDENTS ANNUALLY TO DEVELOP PRACTICAL SKILLS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE–DRIVEN PROTEIN DESIGN, MOLECULAR DYNAMICS, QUANTUM AND SEMI-EMPIRICAL CHEMISTRY, GENOMICS, MATHEMATICAL MODELING, AND DEEP-LEARNING BIOINFORMATICS. THESE COMPETENCIES NOT ONLY ACCELERATE RESEARCH DISCOVERIES BUT ALSO PREPARE GRADUATES FOR THE GROWING WORKFORCE DEMANDS IN BIOTECHNOLOGY, PHARMACEUTICAL DEVELOPMENT, AND DATA SCIENCE. THE POWERWULF™ ZXR1 HPC ENGINE WILL BE HOUSED IN THE CSU DOMINGUEZ HILLS DATA CENTER, MANAGED BY THE CSUDH IT DEPARTMENT AND ADMINISTERED DAY-TO-DAY BY DR. ADEKUNLE AINA. AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE WILL ENSURE BROAD ACCESS, WHILE STRUCTURED COURSEWORK AND REGULAR WORKSHOPS WILL SUSTAIN AND EXPAND INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS, DRIVING INNOVATION AND EXCELLENCE IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATION.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: The National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS) supports basic research that increases our understanding of biological processes and lays the foundation for advances in disease diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. NIGMS also supports research in specific clinical areas that affect multiple organ systems: anesthesiology and peri-operative pain; clinical pharmacology common to multiple drugs and treatments; and injury, critical illness, sepsis, and wound healing. NIGMS-funded scientists investigate how living systems work at a range of levels—from molecules and cells to tissues and organs—in research organisms, humans, and populations. Additionally, to ensure the vitality and continued productivity of the research enterprise, NIGMS provides leadership in supporting the training of future scientists and developing research capacity throughout the country.
